Washington DC, September 14, 2026--The LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index for September 2026 is at 50.5. Fielded from August 21 – September 1, 2026, the Index is up 1.1 points from last month.

The index has alternated gains and losses for the past four months. It now sits 1.9 points below its reading from this time last year. [...] This survey was fielded between August 21 and September 1, 2026. The sample includes 1,000 Americans aged 18-74.

Consumer sentiment has dropped in September, according to the initial reading of the University of Michigan’s monthly survey.

The survey’s index stands at 47.8, versus the 51.7 recorded at the end of August. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a reading of 51.4.

results.content: WASHINGTON, Sept 11 (Reuters) - U.S. consumer prices accelerated in August, while a key measure of underlying inflation posted its largest increase in four months, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest ​rates next week. The two reports led economists to think that PCE inflation excluding the volatile food and energy categories picked up in August. Most economists said the firmer inflation readings, combined with signs of the labor market regaining its footing in August, would compel Fed officials to ​raise borrowing costs not only next Wednesday, but possibly again in October or December. results.content: We're about to find out if inflation outpaced wage growth for the fifth month in a row. The Bureau of Labor Statistics is set to release new consumer price index data at 8:30 a.m. ET. Inflation ticked down from 3.5% to 3.4% in July, and economists expect August's rate to be unchanged, meaning it would remain higher than wage growth. If elevated inflation doesn't slow further amid better-than-expected job growth and persistently low unemployment, that could mean it's time for the first interest-rate hike since 2023.
